records.source: THE VIEW IS PART OF THE GATE. An outline on the screen means nothing without the camera it was drawn through, so the gate carries the camera as ``projection``: a 4 x 4 matrix taking a measurement ``(x, y, z, 1)`` to homogeneous view coordinates ``(sx, sy, depth, sw)``, scaled so that ``sw`` is positive in front of the camera. The outline lives in ``(sx / sw, sy / sw)``. Rows one, two and four are the whole of what :meth:`mask` needs, so re-applying a saved gate needs no plotting library and gives the same answer on any machine; the depth row only lets the outline be drawn back into the volume from another angle.
records.context: The view is part of the data-selection boundary. An outline on the screen means nothing without the camera it was drawn through, so the data-selection boundary carries the camera as ``projection``: a 4 x 4 matrix taking a measurement ``(x, y, z, 1)`` to homogeneous view coordinates ``(sx, sy, depth, sw)``, scaled so that ``sw`` is positive in front of the camera. The outline lives in ``(sx / sw, sy / sw)``. Rows one, two and four are the whole of what :meth:`mask` needs, so re-applying a saved data-selection boundary needs no plotting library and gives the same answer on any machine; the depth row only lets the outline be drawn back into the volume from another angle.
records.translation: LA VISTA FORMA PARTE DEL GATE. Un contorno en la pantalla no significa nada sin la cámara a través de la cual se dibujó, así que el gate lleva la cámara como ``projection``: una matriz de 4 x 4 que lleva una medición ``(x, y, z, 1)`` a coordenadas homogéneas de vista ``(sx, sy, depth, sw)``, escalada para que ``sw`` sea positivo delante de la cámara. El contorno vive en ``(sx / sw, sy / sw)``. Las filas uno, dos y cuatro son todo lo que necesita :meth:`mask`, de modo que volver a aplicar un gate guardado no necesita ninguna biblioteca de gráficos y da la misma respuesta en cualquier máquina; la fila de profundidad solo permite volver a dibujar el contorno en el volumen desde otro ángulo.

records.source: THE ARITHMETIC IS "OVER", LAYER BY LAYER, FROM THE BOTTOM. The canvas starts black. Each ticked layer, bottom first, is laid on with its opacity ``a``: where it covers, ``out = out * (1 - a) + colour * a``; where it does not, ``out`` is left alone. An image covers every pixel; a mask covers its objects only, so the background of a mask never dims what is under it. The result is rounded to the nearest whole grey level.
records.context: The arithmetic is "OVER", layer by layer, from the bottom. The canvas starts black. Each ticked layer, bottom first, is laid on with its opacity ``a``: where it covers, ``out = out * (1 - a) + colour * a``; where it does not, ``out`` is left alone. An image covers every pixel; a mask covers its objects only, so the background of a mask never dims what is under it. The result is rounded to the nearest whole grey level.
records.translation: LA ARITMÉTICA ES "OVER", CAPA A CAPA, DESDE ABAJO. El lienzo empieza en negro. Cada capa marcada, la de abajo primero, se coloca con su opacidad ``a``: donde cubre, ``out = out * (1 - a) + colour * a``; donde no cubre, ``out`` queda intacto. Una imagen cubre todos los píxeles; una máscara solo cubre sus objetos, así que el fondo de una máscara nunca oscurece lo que tiene debajo. El resultado se redondea al nivel de gris entero más cercano.

records.label: spacr.qt.widgets.measurements_example#1
records.source: The Annotate example (``einarolafsson/spacr-example-annotate``) is a real plate: ``measurements/measurements.db`` with its cell, cytoplasm, nucleus and pathogen tables, and the 2,341 crops under ``data/`` it indexes. Annotate and Classify already fetch it into the shared example plate folder (:func:`spacr.example_archives.example_plate_folder`). Every other screen that opens a measurements database can be shown working on the same plate, so this module fetches it once and hands it to whichever screen asked.
records.context: The Annotate example (``einarolafsson/spacr-example-annotate``) is a real plate: ``measurements/measurements.db`` with its cell, cytoplasm, nucleus and pathogen tables, and the 2,341 extracted image regions under ``data/`` it indexes. Annotate and Classify already fetch it into the shared example plate folder (:func:`spacr.example_archives.example_plate_folder`). Every other application view that opens a measurements database can be shown working on the same plate, so this module fetches it once and hands it to whichever application view asked.
records.translation: El ejemplo de Annotate (``einarolafsson/spacr-example-annotate``) es una placa real: ``measurements/measurements.db`` con sus tablas de célula, citoplasma, núcleo y patógeno, y los 2,341 recortes de ``data/`` a los que remite. Annotate y Classify ya la descargan en la carpeta compartida de la placa de ejemplo (:func:`spacr.example_archives.example_plate_folder`). Cualquier otra pantalla que abra una base de datos de mediciones puede mostrarse trabajando sobre la misma placa, así que este módulo la descarga una vez y se la entrega a la pantalla que la haya pedido.

records.label: spacr.qt.widgets.measurements_example#2
records.source: ONE HELPER, NOT ONE COPY PER SCREEN. The cached-or-download decision, the button's busy state and the failure message are the same for Plate Viewer, Tabulate, Graph Builder and the rest; what differs is only which field is filled and which method opens it. So a screen passes that one difference as a callback and nothing else.
records.context: One helper, not one copy per screen. So a screen passes that one difference as a callback and nothing else.
records.translation: UN SOLO AYUDANTE, NO UNA COPIA POR PANTALLA. La decisión entre caché y descarga, el estado ocupado del botón y el mensaje de fallo son los mismos para Plate Viewer, Tabulate, Graph Builder y los demás; lo único que cambia es qué campo se rellena y qué método lo abre. Así que una pantalla pasa esa única diferencia como callback y nada más.
